# Contradicting Trump, Pope Leo says artificial intelligence safety concerns not ‘fake news’ ## Contradicting Trump, Pope Leo says artificial intelligence safety concerns not ‘fake news’ Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, for example, has warned that within six to 12 months, AI could be capable of leading a swarm of agents that could take over the entire internet.
## The pope says AI is one of the biggest challenges to humanity The pope, who called for robust regulation of AI and a slowdown of the technology in his encyclical “Magnificent Humanity,” is up to speed on developments in the field.
Despite being at the end of a grueling four-day trip to France, Leo noted a news report Monday afternoon about [Nvidia introducing guardrails](https://apnews.com/article/nvidia-ai-agent-artificial-intelligence-safety-3c4d7c1cfde82851c0577d1fa29b8621) into AI.
Leo had identified AI as one of [the biggest challenges to humanity](https://apnews.com/article/pope-leo-vision-papacy-artificial-intelligence-36d29e37a11620b594b9b7c0574cc358) within days of his election and took the unusual step of personally launching his own encyclical alongside Anthropic’s co-founder Christopher Olah at a Vatican event in May.

# Contradicting Trump, Pope Leo says artificial intelligence safety concerns not 'fake news' ## Pope Leo's AI concerns [Pope Leo XIV](https://apnews.com/hub/pope-leo-xiv) said Monday that concerns about artificial intelligence going rogue are not “fake news” and should be taken seriously, insisting that safety issues raised by AI experts should be discussed and acted on.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, for example, has warned that within six to 12 months AI could be capable of leading a swarm of agents that could take over the entire internet.

China 'respects' Trump's decision to refer to artificial intelligence as 'super intelligence'
item.description:
## AG Blanche rejects calls for new AI laws after rogue agents target US government websites Attorney General Todd Blanche rejected calls for additional artificial intelligence regulation Sunday on "Fox & Friends Weekend," arguing that existing laws already give the government the tools it needs to pursue bad actors after reports allege that rogue AI agents targeted [U.S. government websites](https://www.foxnews.com/politics).
## Trump defends AI growth amid concerns over advanced systems: 'I don't worry about it' When asked by Fox News' White House correspondent Aishah Hasnie about reports detailing thousands of problematic [AI incidents](https://www.foxbusiness.com/category/artificial-intelligence) involving Anthropic and OpenAI, Trump said he was not concerned.
## China 'respects' Trump's decision to refer to artificial intelligence as 'super intelligence' ![China 'respects' Trump's decision to refer to artificial intelligence as 'super intelligence'](https://a57.foxnews.com/assets.foxnews.com/liveblog/fn/prod/images/2026/09/624/351/70e06985e053688c8e81206e18d25c8f.jpg?ve=1&tl=1)
Getty Images
China's Foreign Ministry put out a statement Saturday saying it "respects" President Donald Trump opting to rebrand [artificial intelligence](https://www.foxnews.com/politics/trump-flexes-american-power-un-warnings-rivals-around-globe) as "super intelligence."
Throughout the week, Trump has repeatedly said he feels "super intelligence" is a more accurate term because the adjective "artificial" makes AI sound "fake."
